notes.subtitle: From Words to Equations

concepts.title: Choose the unknown
concepts.text: Let x be one quantity and write the others in terms of x.

concepts.title: Number problems
concepts.text: Consecutive numbers: x, x + 1. Consecutive odd or even numbers: x, x + 2. Reciprocal of x: 1/x.

concepts.title: Speed, time and work
concepts.text: Time = distance ÷ speed. Upstream speed = u − v and downstream speed = u + v.

concepts.title: Reject wrong roots
concepts.text: A length, an age, a speed or a count cannot be negative or fractional when the problem does not allow it.

formulas: Upstream speed = u − v, downstream speed = u + v
Cost of one item = total cost ÷ number of items
method: Read the problem and choose x.
Write the condition as an equation.
Change it to ax² + bx + c = 0 and solve.
Check each root against the problem and state the answer with units.

A rectangle has perimeter 34 cm and area 60 cm². Find its sides.
A sum of ₹400 is shared equally. With 10 more people, each gets ₹2 less. Find the number of people.

tips: Use brackets when you subtract fractions with x.
Always state which root you reject and why.

notes.chapter: Ratio and Proportion (Including Properties and Uses)
notes.subtitle: Proportionals, Properties & Componendo–Dividendo

concepts.title: Proportion
concepts.text: a, b, c, d are in proportion when a : b = c : d, that is, ad = bc.

concepts.title: Mean and third proportional
concepts.text: The mean proportional between a and b is √(ab). The third proportional to a and b is b²/a.

concepts.title: Continued proportion
concepts.text: a, b, c are in continued proportion when a/b = b/c, so b² = ac.

concepts.title: Componendo and dividendo
concepts.text: If a/b = c/d, then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d). Use it to solve equations with surds.

formulas: a : b = c : d ⇔ ad = bc
Fourth proportional to a, b, c = bc/a
Duplicate ratio a² : b²; triplicate ratio a³ : b³
method: Put each ratio equal to k when a proof has equal ratios.
Write every variable in terms of k.
Simplify each side separately.
Show that both sides give the same expression.

example.question: Find x if (x + 5)/(x − 5) = 3/1 by componendo and dividendo.

practice.question: Find the fourth proportional to 2, 7, 6.
Find the mean proportional between 9 and 16.
Find the third proportional to 4 and 10.
If a : b = 2 : 3, find (3a + 2b) : (4a − b).
If x/(y + z) = y/(z + x) = z/(x + y), and x + y + z ≠ 0, find each ratio.

tips: Do not cancel terms across a + sign.
In the k-method, substitute and simplify each side alone.
After squaring, check the root in the original equation.

notes.subtitle: Remainders, Factors & Unknown Coefficients

concepts.title: Remainder theorem
concepts.text: When f(x) is divided by x − a, the remainder is f(a). For ax − b, the remainder is f(b/a).

concepts.title: Factor theorem
concepts.text: x − a is a factor of f(x) exactly when f(a) = 0.

concepts.title: Finding a first factor
concepts.text: Try the factors of the constant term: ±1, ±2, ±3, … until f(a) = 0.

concepts.title: Complete factorisation
concepts.text: Divide by the first factor to get a quadratic, then factorise the quadratic.

method: Find the zero of the divisor.
Substitute it in f(x).
Set the result equal to the given remainder (0 for a factor).
Solve for the unknown, or divide to factorise fully.

example.question: Factorise x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6.
steps: f(1) = 1 − 6 + 11 − 6 = 0, so x − 1 is a factor.

practice.question: Find the remainder when x³ + 1 is divided by x − 1.
Is x − 2 a factor of x³ − 8?
Find k if x − 1 is a factor of 2x² + kx + 3.
Factorise x³ + 2x² − x − 2.
Find the remainder when 4x³ − 3x + 1 is divided by 2x + 1.
x − 2 and x + 3 are factors of x³ + px² + qx − 6. Find p and q.

tips: The sign changes: for x + a, use f(−a).
Use synthetic or long division to get the quotient.
Check the final factors by multiplying back.

notes.subtitle: Order, Operations & Multiplication

concepts.title: Matrix and order
concepts.text: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers. A matrix with m rows and n columns has order m × n.

concepts.title: Equality
concepts.text: Two matrices are equal when they have the same order and equal corresponding elements.

concepts.title: Addition and scalar multiple
concepts.text: Add or subtract matrices of the same order element by element. kA multiplies every element by k.

concepts.title: Multiplication
concepts.text: AB exists when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. Each element is a row of A times a column of B.

formulas: Order of AB = (rows of A) × (columns of B)
[a b / c d][p q / r s] = [ap + br, aq + bs / cp + dr, cq + ds]
method: Check the orders first.
For each element of the product, multiply a row by a column and add.
Write the answer in the correct order.
For unknowns, equate the corresponding elements.

practice.question: Write the order of [1 2 3].
Find A² for A = [0 1 / 1 0].
Find x and y if [x 1 / 2 y][1 / 2] = [5 / 8].

tips: Check that the product is defined before you multiply.
Keep the order of multiplication: AB and BA can differ.
Write each step of row × column clearly.

notes.subtitle: General Term, Sum & Applications

concepts.title: Arithmetic progression
concepts.text: A list in which each term after the first is found by adding a fixed number d (the common difference).

concepts.title: General term
concepts.text: The nth term is tₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

concepts.title: Sum of n terms
concepts.text: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] = n/2 (a + l), where l is the last term.

concepts.title: Three terms in AP
concepts.text: Take a − d, a, a + d when the sum of three terms is given.

method: Write a and d from the question.
Use tₙ for a single term and Sₙ for a sum.
Form an equation in the unknown and solve it.
Check that n is a natural number.

example.question: Find the 15th term and the sum of 15 terms of 4, 9, 14, ….

Find the 12th term of 2, 5, 8, ….

Which term of 5, 8, 11, … is 92?
Find the sum of 3 + 7 + 11 + … + 99.

tips: n must be a natural number.
Use a − d, a, a + d for three terms.
For a decreasing AP, d is negative.
